title: Optimize span pruning and sampling telemetry to cut tracing CPU overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Tracing instrumentation across the runtime is adding variable CPU overhead (observed up to 9-12% on tail workloads) and increased network egress due to unpruned spans. Current adaptive/tail sampling prototypes reduce data volume but leave expensive span packaging and tag extraction in hot paths. Goal: implement span-level pruning and lightweight sampling telemetry to reduce runtime CPU and network cost while preserving actionable tail traces for SLO investigations. Deliverables: (1) span pruning layer that drops nonessential tag sets and child spans before serialization; (2) a lightweight sampling shim that marks traces for full retention based on early indicators (error tag, latency thresholds, custom predicates) and otherwise emits compact sampled-span summaries; (3) new tracing metrics and dashboards to measure sampling effectiveness, overhead, and retention rate; (4) rollout plan with feature flags and canarying across Dedicated and Hosted clusters.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end CPU overhead attributable to tracing on representative tail-preserving workload reduced to <= 3% (from baseline 9-12%)
Network bytes emitted for tracing down by >= 60% on p95 workloads without loss of full-trace captures for errors/regressions
New metrics available in the Console: tracing.span_pruned_rate, tracing.sampled_full_rate, tracing.sampled_summary_rate, tracing.overhead_cpu_pct
Canary rollout completed with no CUSTOMER-facing error increase; automated rollback triggers on 2x baseline error rate or 1.5x latency P99
Documentation and migration guide published (Confluence) and SDK compatibility notes added to README
tasks: Design span pruning rules and whitelist of preserved tags (Maya)
Prototype lightweight sampling shim in runtime agent (Liam)

Instrument OTel collector to accept compact summaries and full traces (Telemetry team)

Create feature flag and canary runbook; schedule Dedicated cluster canary (SRE)
Write migration and SDK compatibility notes; update public docs
notes: 2026-02-16: Initial perf run using upsampled dev traffic showed 11% CPU overhead when tracing all spans with full tags (baseline: runtime-1.20).

2026-02-20: Design review decided to favor deterministic pruning rules + allow per-customer overrides via sampling policy. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Span+Pruning+Design
2026-02-25: Spike prototype reduced encoded payload per trace by ~68% by removing debug tags and coalescing repeated child spans. Microbench: CPU dropped to ~4.5% on same workload.

2026-03-01: Added early-indicator predicates: error.present, latency_ms>1500, kvcache.miss_rate>0.2; traces flagged by these predicates are retained in full; all others are emitted as trace summaries.
2026-03-03: PR #4125 opened with runtime agent shim and unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4125

2026-03-04: QA smoke tests in staging show regression-free behavior for general traffic; observed reduction in trace bytes of 62% on p95 simulated traffic. Need broader canary before Dedicated rollout.

Follow-ups: add customer-exposed toggle for aggressive pruning, add sampling-policy telemetry for per-customer retention audits, and integrate with billing signals to pass savings to customers as cost-optimized configs.
